item.title: Gold plunges 3% to one-year low as hawkish Fed lifts dollar, yields
item.description: Gold fell below $3,800 an ounce for the first time since September 2025 as expectations of further Federal Reserve rate hikes strengthened the dollar and Treasury yields. Spot gold dropped 3% to $3,736.06, while silver, platinum and palladium also declined sharply.
item.dc:creator: ETMarkets.com
item.content:encoded: Gold plunged to its lowest level in more than a year on Wednesday as hawkish Federal Reserve signals strengthened expectations of further interest-rate increases, lifting the dollar and Treasury yields, Bloomberg News reported.Spot gold fell 3% to $3,736.06 an ounce at 11:43 a.m. ET after touching $3,734.76 earlier in the session, its lowest level since September 26, 2025. US gold futures for December delivery dropped 3.2% to $3,739 an ounce.The metal fell below $3,800 for the first time since September 2025 and was heading for a third consecutive session of losses.“We believe the selloff reflects mounting pressure from a strengthening US dollar, rising Treasury yields and expectations of further monetary tightening. Yesterday’s economic figures reinforced this sentiment,” Naeem Aslam, chief investment officer at Zaye Capital Markets, told Reuters.The dollar rose to a fresh 19-month high as hawkish remarks from Fed officials and recent economic data reinforced expectations of an interest-rate increase next month.For live updates on US Markets, click hereFed Governor Christopher Waller said Wednesday that the central bank needed to respond more aggressively to inflation by either raising rates by half a percentage point in December or signalling a faster pace of increases in 2027.New York Fed President John Williams said Tuesday that the central bank still had work to do to return inflation to its 2% target. St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said the economy would probably require “several interest-rate increases” before spring.Markets see a 92% probability of a 25-basis-point increase in December and an 8% chance of a larger 50-basis-point move, according to the CME FedWatch tool. They are also pricing in quarter-point increases in January and by April.Expectations of tighter policy have pushed the benchmark 10-year Treasury yield toward its longest stretch above 5% in nearly two decades. Higher yields increase the opportunity cost of holding non-interest-bearing assets such as gold.The stronger dollar also makes bullion more expensive for buyers using other currencies.“It is a tough environment for gold, particularly with buying interest still subdued,” said Christopher Wong, a strategist at Oversea-Chinese Banking Corp, to Bloomberg. He said the market would remain cautious without a clear catalyst for a reversal.Gold has lost more than a quarter of its value since the US-Iran war began in late February. The conflict has pushed energy prices higher, fueled inflation and prompted central banks to tighten monetary policy.Investors are now awaiting minutes from the Fed’s October 27-28 meeting for further clues about the rate path. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh avoided directly addressing monetary policy earlier this week, consistent with his stated preference not to provide near-term rate guidance.“If the minutes reinforce concerns about persistent inflation and support additional tightening, Treasury yields and the dollar could strengthen further, potentially extending gold’s decline below $3,800,” Aslam added.Other precious metals also fell sharply. Spot silver declined 5.3% to $44.88 an ounce after touching its lowest level since September 26, 2025.Platinum dropped 4.6% to $1,363.50 after hitting its lowest level since September 17, 2025, extending its year-to-date loss to 33%. Palladium fell 2.6% to $945.95, its lowest level since early November.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

item.title: HFCL, Sterlite Tech shares rally 5% each as Nvidia’s strong earnings eclipse AI worries
item.description: HFCL and Sterlite Technologies shares rally 5% each as Nvidia's better-than-expected earnings and revenue outlook revive optimism around AI infrastructure spending. The gains follow a decline of more than 10% in both stocks over two sessions. Investors are also assessing concerns around US data centre expansion and AI sector valuations.
item.dc:creator: Veer Sharma
item.content:encoded: Shares of optical fibre manufacturers HFCL and Sterlite Tech, whose products are extensively used in AI infrastructure, rallied 5% each on Wednesday after AI bellwether Nvidia reported third-quarter earnings and revenue above Wall Street expectations and issued a fourth-quarter revenue forecast that exceeded analyst estimates. Nvidia shares gained over 5% in after-hours trading.The gains also came after shares of the two companies fell more than 10% over two days, suggesting value buying at lower levels. The uptick also came despite concerns that the Democratic Party's victory in the US midterm elections could bring tighter restrictions on data centre expansion, potentially slowing the development of the country's AI infrastructure.Nvidia's strong earnings are positive for HFCL and Sterlite Tech because they reinforce expectations of sustained AI infrastructure spending globally. This benefits HFCL and Sterlite Tech because AI data centres require extensive optical fibre networks for high-speed, low-latency data transmission and connectivity between servers and facilities.Nvidia's results came as investors continued to assess the company's leadership transition following the departure of longtime CEO Jensen Huang. Nvidia said it would not entertain questions about Huang's resignation and had no plans to reinstate him.Interim CEO Colette Kress told investors that the company expects revenue to grow 75% in fiscal 2028.For the fourth quarter, Nvidia projected revenue of $126 billion to $134 billion, comfortably ahead of the average analyst estimate of just over $125 billion, according to LSEG data. The company clarified that its forecast did not factor in any data centre chip sales to China.“Our momentum is real. NVIDIA is an exceptional technology leader, powered by the relentless innovation of our people,” Kress said.Sensex, Nifty today; Catch all the LIVE stock market updates here Where is AI headed?The data centre slowdown due to the political shift is going to be real, and the earnings estimates behind the valuations that were the cornerstone of bullish arguments are no longer valid, according to Michael O’Rourke at JonesTrading.“Investors have no idea where those estimates will reset,” he said. “As a result, they are de-risking until clarity returns, which won’t be for some time.”Where this differs from a regular sell-off is that we are not seeing recoveries after significant losses, such as Intel Corp. falling further this week even after plunging almost 30% on Friday, according to Jakub Rochlitz at eToro. There’s also increasing cross-sector correlation and a rise in volatility, meaning that the rout is spreading across the market.“The all-or-nothing mentality is surprising to us, because we believe the real truth is more nuanced,” said Chris Zaccarelli at Northlight Asset Management. “We do agree that sentiment has shifted and building data centres will become more difficult, but if there is a productive business case for building them, then they will get built.”The next major indicator of investor appetite for the AI sector will come from Anthropic, which is preparing to set the price of its shares later on Wednesday ahead of its market debut. The listing could value the company at as much as $1.4 trillion. Anthropic has indicated that it is targeting an IPO price at the upper end of its range or potentially above it, Bloomberg News reported.Disclaimer: This article has been written by Veer Sharma, who is not a SEBI-registered Research Analyst or an Investment Adviser.
